content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has convened a Guideline Development Group to address country pharmaceutical pricing policies. The primary goal of WHO guidelines is to serve its Member States by providing recommendations that enhance the health and well-being of populations globally or within specific regions or countries. Conflicts of interest arise when an individual’s secondary interests—such as personal research goals, advocacy for specific conditions, or financial incentives—conflict with the primary objective of improving public health. While secondary interests are often legitimate, they can pose risks if they influence decisions that undermine the primary goal. To enhance transparency, WHO discloses the names and brief biographies of individuals being considered for participation in its Guideline Development Groups. This information is provided by the experts themselves, and WHO is not responsible for its accuracy or completeness. WHO reserves the right to discuss the information with relevant experts and take appropriate actions based on its policies. Participation in a WHO-convened Guideline Development Group does not imply that the views of the experts necessarily reflect WHO’s official policies or decisions. Experts Being Considered for the Guideline Development Group: 1. Lisa Bero Affiliation: University of Sydney, The Cochrane Collaboration Degrees: BSc, PhD Residence: Sydney, Australia Biography: Professor Lisa Bero is Chair of Medicines Use and Health Outcomes at the University of Sydney. She is an internationally recognized researcher in evidence-based healthcare, focusing on the integrity of clinical and basic research evidence used to shape health policy. She leads the Evidence, Policy, and Influence Collaborative, which explores bias reduction in evidence synthesis and pharmaceutical policy. She is also a Senior Editor for Cochrane Public Health and Health Systems. 2. Yingyao Chen Affiliation: Fudan University Degrees: BMed, MSc, PhD Residence: Shanghai, China Biography: Professor Yingyao Chen is a health services expert at Fudan University, where he directs the Key Lab of Health Technology Assessment and the WHO Collaborating Center for Health Technology Assessment. His work focuses on health technology assessment, health policy, and health economics. He also serves as Vice Chairman of several national health committees in China. 3. Amadou Moctar Dièye Affiliation: Ministère de la Santé et de l'Action Sociale, Senegal; Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar Degrees: Doctorate in Pharmacy, Advanced Studies in Pharmacology, Doctorate ès Sciences Residence: Dakar, Senegal Biography: Professor Amadou Moctar Dièye is the Director of Laboratories at Senegal’s Ministry of Health and a pharmacology professor. His expertise includes promoting generic medicines, clinical trials, pharmacovigilance, and anti-doping policies. 4. Andrew Hill Affiliation: University of Liverpool Degrees: PhD Residence: Liverpool, United Kingdom Biography: Dr. Andrew Hill specializes in treatment access issues and drug production costs for HIV, viral hepatitis, tuberculosis, and cancer. He advises WHO, UNITAID, and the Clinton Foundation. 5. Tanya Potashnik Affiliation: Patented Medicines Prices Review Board, Government of Canada Degrees: BA (Economics and Business), MA (Economics) Residence: Ottawa, Canada Biography: Tanya Potashnik is the Director of Policy and Economic Analysis for Canada’s pharmaceutical pricing regulator. With over 25 years of experience, she has played a key role in implementing health technology assessment (HTA) and regulatory changes to lower drug costs in Canada. 6. Shadi Saleh Affiliation: American University of Beirut, Lebanon Degrees: BS, MPublicHealth, PhD Residence: Beirut, Lebanon Biography: Professor Shadi Saleh is the Founding Director of the Global Health Institute and an expert in healthcare financing and evidence-based decision-making. He advises WHO, the World Bank, and the UN on health system strengthening. 7. Vania Cristina Canuto Santos Affiliation: Ministério da Saúde, Brazil Degrees: MSc Residence: Brasília, Brazil Biography: Vania Cristina Canuto Santos is a health economist and Director at Brazil’s National Commission for Health Technologies Incorporation. She has extensive experience in pharmaceutical price regulation and health technology assessment. 8. Sakthivel Selvaraj Affiliation: Public Health Foundation of India Degrees: PhD Residence: New Delhi, India Biography: Dr. Sakthivel Selvaraj is a Director and Professor specializing in health economics and access to medicines. He has contributed to India’s Universal Health Coverage policies and pharmaceutical financing reforms. 9. Netnapis Suchonwanich Affiliation: Ministry of Public Health, Thailand Residence: Nonthaburi, Thailand Biography: Netnapis Suchonwanich is an advisor to Thailand’s Health Intervention and Technology Assessment Program. She played a pivotal role in developing the country’s Universal Health Coverage Scheme and health insurance systems. 10. Fatima Suleman Affiliation: University of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa Degrees: BPharm, MPharm, PhD Residence: Durban, South Africa Biography: Professor Fatima Suleman is a pharmaceutical policy expert and Chair of South Africa’s Pricing Committee for Medicines. She has advised WHO and served on several essential medicines committees. 11. Sabine Vogler Affiliation: Austrian Public Health Institute Degrees: Mag. rer. soc., PhD Residence: Vienna, Austria Biography: Dr. Sabine Vogler is the Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Pharmaceutical Pricing and Reimbursement Policies. She has led numerous research projects on pharmaceutical pricing and access issues in Europe. 12. Jo Watson Affiliation: Australian Government Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee Residence: Sydney, Australia Biography: Jo Watson is the Deputy Chair of Australia’s Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee and a long-standing advocate for consumer health and access to medicines. 13. Rasha Ziada Affiliation: Ministry of Health, Egypt Degrees: BPharm, Dipl. Clin. Pharm, MHealthEcon Residence: Cairo, Egypt Biography: Rasha Ziada is the Chairperson of Egypt’s Central Administration of Pharmaceutical Affairs. She leads committees on drug pricing, registration, and pharmacoeconomics.
